jobs.excerpt: As a Strategic Account Associate, you will support and help manage strategic client accounts while partnering closely with Strategic Account Managers and/or Strategic Account Directors.
jobs.description:
As a Strategic Account Associate, you will support and help manage strategic client accounts while partnering closely with Strategic Account Managers and/or Strategic Account Directors. You will contribute to strategic planning, manage day-to-day client communications, and help ensure work is delivered on time, on budget, and aligned with client goals.

In this role, you will help develop annual strategic and tactical plans, oversee project execution, and proactively identify opportunities to enhance client success. You will also support account financial management by assisting with scoping, budgeting, forecasting, and monitoring team efficiency. Over time, SAAs are expected to increase ownership of client relationships and play an integral role in driving account growth and client advocacy.

Key Responsibilities

Client Strategy & Relationship Management

  • Serve as day-to-day client contact on assigned accounts, in partnership with senior account leadership
  • Develop a strong understanding of clients’ business goals, challenges, and strategic priorities
  • Help translate client vision into actionable plans and high-quality deliverables
  • Contribute to annual strategic and tactical plans, brand plans, and project-level planning
  • Build trust with clients through strong communication, responsiveness, and strategic thinking
  • Proactively offer ideas and recommendations to improve brand performance and client engagement

Account & Business Management

  • Support scoping of work, development of budgets, and ongoing management of account finances
  • Monitor budgets and team efficiency to ensure work is delivered within scope; help flag when requests are out of scope
  • Assist with forecasting planned work and resources; flag risks or changes to leadership
  • Identify potential growth opportunities and new business ideas and share with the account team

Cross-Functional Leadership & Execution

  • Partner with program management to develop project briefs and lead or support kickoff meetings
  • Coordinate internal teams to ensure alignment on strategy, timelines, and client expectations
  • Support quality of deliverables by reviewing for accuracy and readiness before client delivery, while collaborating with senior account team members on final approval
  • Help manage workload and prioritization to keep projects moving and self and team members billable
  • Participate in, and at times lead, client meetings, status calls, and planning calls with healthcare professionals
  • Flag team issues and provide details to support difficult conversations related to timelines, budgets, and feedback

Professional Development & Industry Awareness

  • Stay current on industry trends, scientific developments, and competitive landscapes relevant to clients
  • Continuously build strategic, financial, and client management skills
  • Act as a strong ambassador for Precision AQ internally and externally

Additional Responsibilities

  • Stay abreast of developments (eg, science, competitors, regulations) in clients’ industries
  • Keep honing marketing and strategy expertise to better serve clients and Precision AQ
  • Network and connect to grow your influence and add value

Support of the Strategic Account Director or Strategic Account Manager may include tasks, such as: assisting in the preparation of annual strategic/tactical plans for clients and Precision AQ, addressing ad hoc client requests and needs, reviewing and finalizing materials for distribution to the client or other external parties, participating in and/or leading calls with clients or healthcare practitioners, preparing content as necessary to fulfill client requirements, traveling to and attending and supporting live meetings with clients and/or healthcare practitioners, and more. The day-to-day activities of a SAA will vary greatly depending on client needs, account size, product status, and Precision AQ needs.

Desired Skills

We seek highly motivated people with outstanding professional credentials, business accomplishment, and leadership. In addition, we place high value on relevant personal qualities: resourcefulness, tenacity, independence, energy, and self-confidence.

Qualifications

  • Minimum required: Bachelor’s degree required
  • Other Required: At least 1-year account management experience within the medical communications or related industry
  • Preferred: Advanced degree (PhD, MD, or PharmD) in life sciences, pharmacy, medicine, and/or advanced degree in management, marketing, or business preferred

Skills

  • PowerPoint design proficiency
  • Strong strategic and analytical background
  • Strong desire to learn in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong communication and presentation skills

jobs.excerpt: Say hello to HagertyHagerty is a company built by drivers for drivers.
jobs.description:
Say hello to Hagerty

Hagerty is a company built by drivers for drivers. We put our members at the center of everything we do and are dedicated to making it easier and more enjoyable for enthusiasts to drive and celebrate the machines they love. We’re proud to be the world’s largest insurer of collectible and enthusiast vehicles and are home to the Hagerty Drivers Club, the world’s largest car club. Our Marketplace business presents live and digital sales across the U.S. and Europe, we host a number of driving events and concours, and our award-winning automotive journalists produce the most popular car magazine globally, alongside internationally awarded videos. We’re committed to Never Stop Driving. Ready to get in the driver’s seat? Join us! 

As a Solution Architect II, you will join us in creating software solutions that are well designed and take a long term strategic view. By considering the impact of design choices today against an understanding of a software product’s strategic direction, our solution architects seek to limit future constraints and provide the correct amount of flexibility while delivering business value with timely releases. The team achieves this by placing business capabilities into Hagerty’s Technology Portfolio of Software Assets, by architecting software services, designing APIs, and maintaining clear bounded contexts between each. As excellent communicators and leaders within the organization, they ensure all audiences are aligned on why our software solutions are required, how they are implemented, and what they achieve.

What you’ll do

Own and maintain bounded contexts between software product domains in our Technology Portfolio by-

  • Acting as a subject matter expert on 1-3 complex domains within our business
  • Building shared understanding around the encapsulation and distinct purposes of your domains
  • Decomposing new business concepts and capabilities into bounded contexts
  • Creating and maintaining context maps that detail your context’s interactions with others in the Portfolio

Design and own inter-context communication specifications that serve the needs of the business now and in the future by-

  • Designing HTTP APIs and messages that provide solutions to business capabilities and product features
  • Deciding whether to extend, refactor, or build new software
  • Establishing strong domain concepts in your API resources that can evolve naturally, over narrow bespoke solutions
  • Writing excellent design artifacts (OpenAPI, etc.) that make solutions simple to implement and easy to test

Elevate the communication of the enterprise around technology and how it serves our strategy by-

  • Explaining technical concepts and solutions to nontechnical stakeholders both ad-hoc and by publishing solution artifacts
  • Championing the capabilities of your product domain(s) to stakeholders and other product teams
  • Informing product decision making via your technical knowledge and experience creating software

Mature Architectural thinking at Hagerty by-

  • Evaluating tradeoffs in solution design (e.g. speed, technical debt, vendor cost, complexity) and documenting how you reached your decisions
  • Being opinionated on implementation based on your knowledge of your product’s roadmaps and the business’ strategy
  • Measuring architectural maturity in the product contexts you support, and proposing ways to improve that maturity by working with Application Architecture and Engineering
  • Publishing and adopting common integration patterns between contexts that can be easily re-used by other architects and teams

This might describe you

You’re a talented communicator

  • You meet people where they are and then build shared understanding
  • Comfortable and effective explaining technical concepts to audiences of varying level and technical skill
  • Lead and contribute to discussions around product design per business strategy
  • Bias towards creating visual artifacts that represent contexts, designs, and shared understanding
  • You enjoy learning and then sharing what you’ve learned with others
  • You write effectively about how software works

You have a breadth of experience building software

· Programming languages

· Deployment

· Databases/Persistence

· Patterns and anti-patterns

You have a Fundamental knowledge of technology concepts

· API Design

· HTTP Communication

· ReST/RPC Styles

  • Data movement-- polling, eventing, messaging
  • Integration patterns and lifecycle
  • Identity— Authentication and Authorization

You have a growth mindset

  • You recognize that relying on your current knowledge means falling behind, and you treat continuous learning as a professional responsibility
  • You are energized by discovering a tool, pattern, or approach you didn't know existed
  • You share what you’ve learned with the team because you know that communicating what you have learned helps you deepen your own understanding while helping your teammates grow

You have experience being in a visible senior role and want to collaborate with others

You enjoy operating independently, and can concurrently positively impact multiple initiatives with competing priority

You love discovering the actual problem that needs to be solved as much as solving

Pluses

  • You’ve deployed and/or integrated software with the Duck Creek Insurance Platform
  • You’ve read Domain Driven Design by Eric Evans
  • You’re familiar with modeling tools such as C4
  • When there’s no leader in the room, you tend to take the lead rather than wait
  • You’re comfortable in front of audiences of all sizes

· You’ve written .NET code

  • You’ve designed and released APIs with both ReST and RPC styles
  • You love creating excellent API documentation with tools like OpenAPI

Other things to note

  • This position is open to U.S. remote work. However, team members who reside within 20 miles of the Traverse City headquarters will follow a hybrid schedule, working from the office three days per week.
  • May require travel for quarterly events.
  • Familiarity with public company requirements, including Sarbanes Oxley and key regulations, if applicable. jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

‎

The Director, Strategic Finance will be a senior thought partner to leaders across Millennium, translating complex financial, medical claims, clinical, and operational data into decisions that drive growth and performance. The role will evaluate strategic investments, strengthen forecasting and decision support, improve the economics of value-based care, and help leaders understand where to allocate resources for the greatest impact. This is a hands-on role for someone who combines rigorous financial analysis with an operator mindset and enjoys moving from insight to action.

WHY THIS ROLE

  • Enterprise visibility: Work on high-priority decisions spanning growth, market performance, physician economics, care delivery, and resource allocation.
    •Strategic + operating breadth: Move between business cases, forecasting, payer and risk economics, provider performance, and execution tracking.
    •Platform scale: Join Millennium during a period of continued expansion, with access to the capabilities and learning opportunities of a broader national care delivery platform.
    •Build and influence: Strengthen the models, metrics, and decision processes leaders use to run the business and measure value creation.

    ‎

    How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as a strategic finance partner to senior leaders across finance, operations, clinical, network, and growth teams, bringing a fact-based financial perspective to key business decisions.
  • Build and own driver-based financial models for growth initiatives, market expansion, physician partnerships, service-line opportunities, care programs, and other strategic investments; frame returns, risks, sensitivities, and trade-offs.
  • Analyze performance across markets, practices, providers, service lines, and patient populations by connecting P&L, claims, utilization, quality, and operational data to explain trends and identify opportunities.
  • Support value-based and risk-based arrangements by evaluating medical cost trends, utilization, quality performance, risk adjustment, shared savings, capitation assumptions, benchmarks, and contract economics.
  • Lead business-case development and post-investment tracking, including ROI, cost-benefit, scenario, and variance analysis, to ensure initiatives translate into measurable results.
  • Support annual planning, rolling forecasts, and long-range financial planning; improve the quality of assumptions, driver visibility, and accountability across the organization.
  • Partner with clinical, care management, network, and operations teams to identify, size, prioritize, and track opportunities that improve performance and reduce avoidable utilization and total cost of care.
  • Translate complex analysis into concise, executive-ready insights and recommendations for senior leadership, provider-facing teams, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Develop scalable reporting, KPI frameworks, and decision-support tools that increase transparency, accelerate decision-making, and strengthen financial discipline as the organization grows.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, Healthcare Administration, Analytics, or a related field; MBA or other advanced degree is a plus.
  • 7+ years of experience in strategic finance, FP&A, corporate development, investment banking, management consulting, healthcare finance/analytics, or a similarly rigorous analytical role.
  • Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including the ability to build driver-based forecasts, investment cases, scenarios, and executive-level decision support from imperfect or complex data.
  • Advanced Excel proficiency. Experience with SQL/Databricks and visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau is helpful but not required for the right finance leader.
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information into clear business recommendations, communicate with senior executives, and influence cross-functional teams without relying on formal authority.
  • High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities evolve and the finance team is expected to help shape the answer - not simply report the result.

WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

  • Experience in physician organizations, MSOs/IPAs, health plans, risk-bearing entities, or other value-based care models, with a strong understanding of utilization, medical cost, capitation, and total cost of care.
  • A track record of pairing financial rigor with commercial and operating judgment - and of staying close enough to execution to understand whether the expected value is actually being realized.
  • Experience supporting multi-site growth, market expansion, partnerships, acquisitions/integrations, or other scaled healthcare delivery initiatives.
  • The range to move comfortably from detailed analysis to an executive narrative: you can interrogate a model, challenge assumptions, and then explain the answer simply and persuasively.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Senior leaders have a clearer, faster view of the economic drivers behind performance and the actions that can change the trajectory.
  • Major growth and operating initiatives are supported by rigorous business cases, explicit assumptions, and disciplined follow-through on realized value.
  • Forecasting and performance management become more driver-based, connected to operating realities, and useful as decision tools rather than reporting exercises.
  • Financial, claims, and operational insights consistently translate into practical actions that improve growth, provider performance, affordability, and patient outcomes.

What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role

The VP of Revenue Enablement is a new, dedicated leadership role for Parachute's Enablement function, reporting to the EVP of Revenue Operations as a peer to the leaders of Revenue Operations, Revenue Systems, and Data Analysis.

You'll take over Parachute's existing Enablement team and the programs already in flight, and build from there into a durable, well-resourced function with a clear operating model and a real seat in how Parachute plans and runs go-to-market. You'll have latitude to shape the team as the function matures.

This role exists to grow the business: build a team of effective, efficient sellers and sales leaders, and put in place the training, content, coaching, and tools that make every seller and partner productive faster. Revenue Enablement sits inside Revenue Operations and plugs directly into how Parachute sells — our BDR and AE teams across all four sales motions (Supplier, Health System, Clinician Activation, and Payor), the external supplier reps who sell Parachute on our behalf, our Customer Success and Account Management teams, and the Marketing and Product Marketing functions that support them.

What You'll Do

Build and lead the team

  • Directly manage and develop Parachute's Enablement Directors, building the operating rhythm, goals, and career growth this function hasn't had until now.
  • Hire, onboard, and develop future enablement team members as the function scales alongside the broader go-to-market org.
  • Set the standard for enablement excellence at Parachute — coach your own team the way you expect them to coach sellers and sales leaders.

Own the enablement program

  • Take ownership of the pillars defined in Parachute's Enablement Program, turning each from a design document into a living, resourced program across all four core sales motions — Supplier, Health System, Clinician Activation, and Payor.
  • Own new-hire onboarding and ramp across our internal seller-facing roles, BDR and AE, with the explicit goal of cutting time-to-first-deal and time-to-quota.
  • Own seller productivity as an ongoing metric, not just a ramp-period concern: activity quality, pipeline generation, and quota attainment by rep, team, and motion.
  • Drive rep-side HubSpot adoption — the habits, hygiene, and consistent usage across our sales motions that make pipeline data something the rest of the business can trust.
  • Build and maintain the playbooks that run our day-to-day motion, including the Lead Attack speed-to-lead playbooks.

Enable partners and the channel

  • Own the SSR (Supplier Sales Rep) program — external supplier reps who sell Parachute on our behalf, with their own curriculum, certification, and materials built for that audience rather than repurposed from internal training.
  • Build a dedicated Channel Enablement track for the wider partner ecosystem, so partners represent Parachute accurately and consistently.
  • Measure partner-sourced activity and productivity with the same rigor applied to our own sellers.

Build the content and certification system

  • Build a content architecture that gets sellers and partners the right asset at the right moment, replacing one-off requests and tribal knowledge with a real system.
  • Design certification programs for every seller-facing role, not just new hires, so skill and product knowledge stay current as Parachute's platform evolves.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Product, and Revenue Operations to keep messaging, positioning, and talk tracks current as the platform and market evolve.

Coach performance, not just training

  • Run a regular cadence of call reviews, deal coaching, and skill-building grounded in real pipeline and real calls, not generic curriculum.
  • Train the trainers: build frontline sales leaders' own coaching ability, and coach sales leaders directly, so reinforcement happens inside the sales org and doesn't rely solely on Enablement.
  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success leadership to diagnose skill gaps by rep, team, and motion, then build targeted programs to close them.

About Lumistry

The Opportunity

Lumistry is a PE-backed SaaS company (~$40M ARR) serving the pharmacy market. We're building out our accounting function and need a Senior Accountant who owns the full cost side of the ledger and drives a tight 5-day close. You'll partner directly with the Controller and be a key contributor to a lean, high-accountability finance team. This is a high-visibility role - your schedules and reconciliations feed directly into board-level reporting.

What You'll Own

Month-End Close

  • Execute all assigned close tasks within a 5-business-day close calendar
  • Prepare and post journal entries for accruals, prepaids, reclasses, and fixed asset activity
  • Reconcile assigned balance sheet accounts monthly with full support documentation
  • Deliver flux analysis on balance sheet and cost line items - variance explanations ready for Controller review by close Day 5
  • Coordinate with Accounts Payable to ensure cost completeness before books are locked

Balance Sheet Ownership

  • Own the reconciliation suite: accrued liabilities, prepaid expenses, fixed assets, deposits, and other current and non-current balance sheet accounts
  • Maintain fixed asset subledger - additions, disposals, depreciation runs, and physical inventory coordination
  • Manage intercompany account reconciliations across Lumistry's business units; flag and resolve out-of-balance positions before close
  • Keep prepaid schedules current - amortization accuracy and completeness each period

Cost Accounting

  • Track and allocate COGS across product lines; ensure vendor invoices are coded to the correct cost center and GL account
  • Build and maintain vendor accrual schedules - no material unrecorded costs at close
  • Partner with department heads to understand spend timing and flag budget-to-actual variances that need explanation
  • Support the Controller in cost trend analysis for board and investor reporting packages

Accounts Payable & Ramp

  • Serve as the accounting team's primary owner of the Ramp platform - card program reconciliation, expense coding review, and policy exception escalation
  • Review and approve AP coding for accuracy against chart of accounts and cost center structure
  • Ensure vendor bills in NetSuite match POs and receiving documentation; manage discrepancy resolution

NetSuite Administration (Accounting)

  • Maintain chart of accounts integrity - propose and document any additions or changes
  • Run and distribute standard reports; build saved searches and custom reports to support close and analysis needs
  • Identify and escalate workflow inefficiencies; partner with Controller on system optimization

Audit & Compliance

  • Prepare audit-ready support packages for all balance sheet and cost accounts
  • Respond to auditor PBC requests for assigned areas; maintain a clean, organized workpaper structure year-round
  • Ensure documentation standards are met for every journal entry and reconciliation

Cross-Functional

  • Collaborate with FP&A on actuals-to-budget reporting; provide GL-level detail to support variance commentary
  • Partner with HR/Payroll to ensure compensation-related accruals and expense allocations are recorded accurately
  • Support the Controller and CFO on ad hoc analysis, process improvement projects, and due diligence requests

What You Bring

Experience (Required)

  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience
  • 5 years in accounting - you've held an accountant title, not just FP&A or analyst
  • NetSuite experience required; Ramp or comparable T&E/card platform a strong plus
  • Solid grasp of US GAAP, particularly around accruals, prepaids, and fixed assets
  • Proven track record in a fast close environment (5 days or fewer)
  • Detail-oriented with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously
  • Comfortable operating independently in a remote environment - proactive communicator, not a hand-holder

Competencies

  • Technical rigor: you know accruals, prepaids, and fixed assets, and you can support every number in your reconciliations
  • Systems fluency: you're fluent in NetSuite and Ramp, and you spot process improvements even when you're not the one setting policy
  • Judgment under ambiguity: PE-backed SaaS moves fast; you make a sound call, document it, and flag it to leadership
  • Process-minded: you look for manual reconciliations that could be eliminated with better systems, and you raise it

Why Lumistry

  • Direct line to the Controller and CFO - your work lands in board decks
  • Systems investment already made (NetSuite, Ramp) - you're optimizing, not building from scratch
  • PE-backed growth stage - real scope, real visibility
  • Remote-first, high-trust environment

Compensation

Benefits

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a strong technical foundation and practical experience with scripting, automation, and data extraction workflows. Technical Skills (Essential)

  • Proven ability to extract data from complex structures (hierarchies, archived pages, inconsistent HTML)
  • Solid background in data cleaning, normalization, and validation, delivering structured datasets (CSV, JSON, Google Sheets)

Additional requirements

  • Demonstrated experience handling anti-bot mechanisms and dynamic site structures at scale
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or equivalent) and containerization (Docker) as part of real workflows
  • Hands-on experience with LLM frameworks (LangChain, OpenRouter, or similar) applied to automation tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy
  • Self-directed work ethic with ability to troubleshoot independently
  • A link to GitHub is a plus
  • English proficiency: Upper-intermediate (B2) or above (required)

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10–20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active.

On this project, contributors can earn up to $40 per hour equivalent, depending on their level and pace of contribution. jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Services
jobs.excerpt: Engineering Manager, Services Ilir Sela started Slice with the belief that local pizzerias deserve every advantage available to major franchises—without sacrificing their independence.
jobs.description:
Engineering Manager, Services

Ilir Sela started Slice with the belief that local pizzerias deserve every advantage available to major franchises—without sacrificing their independence. What began with his family’s pizzerias now supports tens of thousands of restaurants with the technology, services, and collective power they need to serve modern customers and build lasting businesses. We build for entrepreneurs who put everything into their shops. They deserve technology that is dependable, intuitive, and capable of creating meaningful economic value. We move with urgency, think from first principles, and measure success by the outcomes we create for pizzerias and their customers.

The Challenge to Solve

Slice’s Services teams build the backend systems, APIs, integrations, and operational capabilities that power our platform. We are looking for a high-agency Engineering Manager who can identify the most valuable problems, turn ambiguity into clear direction, and build a team capable of delivering exceptional results. This is not a coordination-only role. You will stay close to the technology, product, and customer. You will be accountable for both your team's performance and the impact it creates. Management is a force multiplier—not another layer of process.

Your role is to create the conditions in which talented engineers can do the best work of their careers. That means setting a clear mission, raising standards, removing obstacles, developing judgment, and holding yourself and others accountable.

Putting people first does not mean avoiding difficult conversations or lowering the bar. It means giving people meaningful ownership, direct feedback, strong support, and the opportunity to grow.

Our strongest managers:

  • Focus teams on customer outcomes rather than activity.
  • Create clarity when the path is uncertain.
  • Make decisions with incomplete information and adapt quickly.
  • Stay close to the details without becoming the bottleneck.
  • Challenge assumptions and look for asymmetric opportunities.
  • Build trust through candor, consistency, and follow-through.
  • Take responsibility for outcomes, including when things go wrong.

The Role

Own customer and business outcomes

Partner with Product, Design, Data, and Operations to identify the problems most worth solving. Define success through measurable value for pizzerias, customers, and the business—not projects completed or code shipped.

Lead technical direction

Guide architecture and engineering decisions across the services your team owns. Help the team balance speed, reliability, simplicity, and long-term system health.

Our services are converging on Python, while parts of our ecosystem use Go and Ruby. We choose technology based on the problem and the customer value it enables—not preference or fashion.

You should be comfortable leading teams working with:

  • Python, Go, and Ruby services.
  • APIs, distributed systems, and asynchronous workflows.
  • Databases, AWS, observability, and production operations.
  • Service migrations, reliability, security, and performance.

Build a high-agency team

Give engineers context, clear decision boundaries, and meaningful ownership. Expect them to move with urgency, exercise judgment, raise issues early, and own what happens in production.

When the team is blocked, work across boundaries and find a path forward rather than simply escalating the problem.

Raise execution standards

Help the team deliver valuable improvements frequently without sacrificing quality. Reduce unnecessary ceremony, make risk visible, and build lightweight mechanisms that improve focus and learning.

Use customer feedback, product data, incidents, and operational metrics to understand whether the team’s decisions are working.

Develop exceptional people

Hire and retain outstanding engineers, including those from unconventional backgrounds who demonstrate unusual ability and drive.

Coach engineers across experience levels, recognize future leaders, reward strong performance, and address underperformance clearly and promptly.

Lead across Slice

Build strong relationships with other engineering, product, and business leaders. Influence through judgment and results rather than hierarchy.

Surface disagreement directly, resolve it constructively, and optimize for Slice and its customers—not only your own team.

The Team

You will lead engineers working on services that power key Slice experiences. The team collaborates across the US, Canada, UK, and North Macedonia, alongside partners in Product, Design, Data, and Operations.

We value thoughtful asynchronous communication, direct discussion, and high-quality written decisions. Geography should not determine who has context, influence, or ownership.

You will report to an Engineering Director and work with other managers and technical leaders to raise the standard across Slice Engineering.

The Winning Recipe

We care more about evidence of impact, judgment, and trajectory than a perfectly conventional background.

Strong candidates will bring:

  • Experience building and operating customer-facing software or platforms.
  • Experience managing high-performing engineering teams.
  • Strong technical judgment across backend services, APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and production operations.
  • Experience with Python, Go, Ruby, or comparable backend technologies.
  • A record of improving both customer outcomes and engineering effectiveness.
  • The ability to turn complex, ambiguous problems into clear direction.
  • A founder-minded approach: resourceful, decisive, intellectually curious, and unwilling to wait for perfect conditions.
  • Strong instincts for leverage—knowing when to move quickly and when deeper investment is necessary.
  • The courage to challenge weak thinking, including your own.
  • Clear, direct communication across technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Low ego, high standards, and a strong sense of personal accountability.

You will be succeeding when:

  • Your team understands the customer outcomes it owns.
  • Engineers operate with increasing independence, judgment, and urgency.
  • Valuable improvements reach customers frequently.
  • Systems become simpler, more reliable, and easier to evolve.
  • High performers are growing and choosing to stay.
  • Performance problems are addressed rather than allowed to compound.
  • Cross-functional partners trust the team to solve difficult problems.
  • Slice creates more value for pizzerias because your team exists.

The Extras

Benefits include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision plans.
  • Flexible working hours.
  • Generous time-off policies.
  • Employee well-being allowance for eligible employees.
  • Market-leading maternity and paternity schemes.

Compensation package: $150k-$175k CAD base, plus benefits. Benefits may vary by location.

The Hiring Process

  1. Application.
  2. 30-minute introductory conversation.
  3. 60-minute conversation with an Engineering Director.
  4. Two leadership and technical interviews with future peers and team members.
  5. Conversation with our Head of RnD.
  6. Offer.

At Slice we are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and supportive workplace. Our core values – We’re doers, Nail the basics, Better together, We’re Pan Atlantic, Build in Public and It’s a pizza Party - guide everything we do, innovate, learn and grow.

Privacy Notice Statement of Acknowledgment

When you apply for a job on this site, the personal data contained in your application will be collected by Slice. Slice is keeping your data safe and secure. Once we have received your personal data, we put in place reasonable and appropriate measures and controls to prevent any accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, or unauthorised access. If selected, we will process your personal data for hiring /employment processes, as well as our legal obligations.

If you are not selected for the job position and you have given consent on the question below (by selecting "Give consent") we will store and process your personal data and submitted documents (CV) to consider eligibility for employment up to 365 days (one year). You have the right to withdraw your previously given consent for storing your personal data and CV in the Slice database considering eligibility for employment for a year. You have the right to withdraw your consent at any time.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to link your passion with a purpose? At NantIQ, we bring together healthcare technology solutions with complementary capabilities and provide the strategy, investment, and connections that help each one thrive. NaviNet® and NaviNet AllPayer®, our payer-provider collaboration solutions, increase operational efficiency, unlock savings, and enhance communications. Eviti®, our evidence-based oncology utilization management solution, helps payers manage costs while ensuring patients receive appropriate, guideline-aligned care. We're seeking innovative thinkers who love doing meaningful work. If you're looking to bring your skills and expertise to a connected network of growing technology companies, it's time for you to join us! To ensure we can provide the best in healthcare tech, we focus on building the best team. Through holding true to our core values — clarity, empathy, collaboration, integrity, a sense of community, and a pioneering approach — we are creating a vibrant culture where ideas can blossom, people can thrive, and success can flourish.

NantIQ is hiring a skilled sales professional to drive sales growth for our NaviNet product line. The Director of Payer Sales will drive growth of NaviNet across large health plans and payer-adjacent organizations by prospecting, developing, and expanding relationships with key decision-makers. This commercially focused leader will leverage deep healthcare payer expertise to identify and cultivate new opportunities, lead consultative sales engagements, and advance complex opportunities from prospecting through close. This role may be right for you if you possess a strong understanding of payer and provider operations, including eligibility and benefits, claims workflows, prior authorization, document exchange, provider engagement, administrative efficiency, and cost reduction. You're skilled at uncovering operational challenges, building trusted relationships with payer stakeholders, and effectively communicating the business value of NaviNet’s solutions. You operate most successfully as a self-directed, results-oriented sales professional and you have a demonstrated history of achieving results and possess the ability to independently manage a sales territory and advance opportunities with limited day-to-day supervision. You're confident being the voice of the customer, bringing market and customer insights to inform sales strategy, product positioning, and innovation while helping advance NantIQ’s mission to improve healthcare connectivity, efficiency, and outcomes. Although this is a remote role, up to 35% travel is anticipated for client engagement, conferences and events as necessary. Travel expectation may vary throughout the course of the year as business needs necessitate.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Develop and execute a strategic, proactive sales strategy to expand NaviNet within new and existing payer relationships and identify, develop, and close new business opportunities across national and regional health plans, managed care organizations, and payer services organizations.
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with key payer stakeholders and senior executives across provider network operations, claims, eligibility and benefits, utilization management, provider relations, digital transformation, interoperability, contact center, procurement, and related functions.
  • Leverage a consultative sales approach to uncover customer needs, operational challenges, and strategic priorities, and effectively position NaviNet’s payer-provider collaboration and administrative workflow solutions to address those needs.
  • Lead complex sales engagements from prospecting and discovery through solution development, presentation, negotiation, contracting, and close, maintaining ownership and momentum throughout the sales cycle.
  • Develop and communicate compelling business cases, account strategies, proposals, and pursuit plans that clearly demonstrate the operational, financial, and strategic value of NaviNet.
  • Negotiate and close complex enterprise agreements, leveraging a proven track record of success selling into large payer organizations and consistently delivering against sales objectives.
  • Establish credibility with senior and C-suite executives by demonstrating a deep understanding of payer operations, provider needs, administrative workflows, healthcare technology, and evolving market dynamics.
  • Partner effectively with Sales, Product, Marketing, Client Success, Implementation, and executive leadership teams to develop customer-specific strategies, coordinate subject matter expertise, and support proposals, contracting, and other deal activities.
  • Independently manage pipeline development, prospecting, outreach, follow-up, CRM activity, forecasting, meeting preparation, and internal coordination with limited day-to-day supervision.
  • Apply strong analytical, strategic thinking, creative problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills to navigate complex customer environments and develop solutions that align payer priorities with NaviNet’s capabilities.
  • Adapt quickly to changing customer needs, market conditions, organizational priorities, and technology environments while effectively managing multiple opportunities and maintaining consistent sales momentum.
  • Maintain current knowledge of healthcare payer and provider operations, interoperability, administrative workflows, digital transformation, and market trends to provide valuable insights and proactive guidance to clients and internal teams.
  • Serve as a strong voice of the customer by bringing market intelligence, customer feedback, and emerging payer and provider needs into NantIQ to inform sales strategy, solution positioning, product development, and innovation.

Education & Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration (sales), Healthcare Administration, Information Technology, Life Sciences, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of progressive sales or business development experience within healthcare software, SaaS, healthcare technology, or related industries, with a proven track record of success selling to large national and regional payer organizations.
  • Demonstrated success in business development, client development, strategic partnerships, account growth, or enterprise sales, with direct experience engaging payer operations, provider relations, network management, claims, utilization management, technology, and other key stakeholders.
  • Proven track record of consistently achieving or exceeding sales goals and delivering measurable results in pipeline growth, revenue generation, account expansion, strategic partnerships, or other meaningful business outcomes.
  • Experience selling SaaS, healthcare technology, payer-provider collaboration, or administrative workflow solutions, preferably supporting eligibility and benefits, claims, prior authorization, provider portals, interoperability, document exchange, provider engagement, workflow automation, or related administrative functions.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Strong understanding of payer and provider operational priorities, including administrative efficiency, reduction of manual transactions, workflow automation, provider experience, call volume reduction, interoperability, compliance, network collaboration, and administrative cost management.
  • Demonstrated ability to build credibility and develop strategic relationships with director, senior director, and executive-level payer stakeholders across operations, provider relations, network management, claims, utilization management, technology, digital transformation, and business functions.
  • Proven ability to manage complex, enterprise-level sales cycles, including prospecting, discovery, solution development, executive presentations, contract negotiation, and closing.
  • Highly self-directed and comfortable managing multiple opportunities, prioritizing activities, maintaining consistent follow-up, and driving next steps with limited day-to-day supervision.
  • Proficient in CRM tools and disciplined in maintaining accurate account records, managing pipeline activity, documenting next steps, forecasting, and providing reliable visibility into opportunity status.
  • Demonstrates strong commercial judgment, including the ability to qualify opportunities, identify and address operational and organizational deal blockers, engage the appropriate internal subject matter expertise, and effectively prioritize resources.
  • Strong communication, organization, presentation, collaboration, curiosity, and follow-through skills, with the ability to adapt to changing customer needs, technology environments, and complex healthcare operations.

The salary range for applicable remote US-based applicants to this position is below. The specific rate will depend on the successful candidate’s qualifications, prior experience as well as geographic location.

  • $95,000 - $109,000 base salary + 50/50 OTE commission opportunity.

We value each of our employee’s total wellness. From robust medical, dental, and vision insurance, to financial planning assistance, to physical and mental wellness discounts, including an optional annual subscription to the Headspace app and unlimited access to our online learning platform, we understand that our company succeeds when our employees succeed as individuals.

jobs.description:
Is it surprising to hear that a financial institution of 1.5 million members and over $30 billion in managed assets say that success comes from focusing on people, not profits?

Our “people helping people” philosophy has guided us since 1935, driving our deep commitment to serving our members, communities, and each other. When you join our team, you become part of a purpose-driven organization where your work makes a real difference.

While we’re proud of our history, we’re even more excited about our future. With business and technology transformation on the horizon, there’s never been a better time to be part of BECU.


You bring more than your expertise to your role, and that matters here. Your story, perspectives, and lived experiences help shape belonging at BECU and deepen how we connect with and support our employees, our members, and our communities.


PAY RANGE

The Target Pay Range for this position is $199,300.00-$243,800.00 annually. The full Pay Range is $155,200.00 - $288,000.00 annually. At BECU, compensation decisions are determined using factors such as relevant job-related skills, experience, and education or training. Should an offer for employment be made, we will consider individual qualifications. In addition to your salary, compensation incentives are available for the hired applicant. Incentives are performance based and targets vary by role.

BENEFITS – because people helping people starts with supporting you

  • 401(k) Company Match (up to 3%)

  • 4% annual contribution to your 401(k) by BECU

  • Medical, Dental and Vision (family contributions as well)

  • PTO Program + Exchange Program

  • Tuition Reimbursement Program

  • BECU Cares volunteer time off + donation match

IMPACT YOU’LL MAKE:

As the Director, Forecasting & Planning, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping BECU's future by helping leaders make informed, data-driven decisions that support growth, financial strength, operational excellence, and exceptional member experiences. You'll bring together financial and operational insights, translating complex business drivers into clear forecasts, strategic plans, and actionable recommendations that guide the organization forward.

In this highly visible leadership role, you'll partner with senior leaders across Finance, Enterprise Strategy, Product, Marketing, Operations, Technology, Treasury, Risk, and other key teams to align resources, priorities, and opportunities with BECU's strategic objectives. Your expertise will help identify emerging trends, anticipate risks, uncover opportunities, and create a forward-looking view of organizational performance.

You'll also build and lead a high-performing forecasting and planning team, establishing scalable planning practices, governance frameworks, and executive reporting capabilities that connect business decisions to meaningful outcomes. Your work will directly influence how BECU plans, invests, grows, and delivers value to our members.

To join our dynamic team in this role, we require candidates to be residents of WA, OR, ID, CA, AZ, TX, NC, SC, GA, or VA. If you’re located in Washington state and within a reasonable driving distance to our Tukwila Headquarters (TFC), we encourage you come into the office on Tuesdays & Wednesdays each week. For those candidates that live outside the commutable distance to TFC and in any of our approved remote work locations, this role will be primarily remote. Remote or onsite, we are committed to ensuring you are fully engaged and included in our collaborative environment.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Shape the Planning Strategy: Develop and lead the vision, operating model, roadmap, planning calendar, standards, and governance framework for forecasting and planning activities, ensuring alignment with enterprise planning processes and divisional priorities.
  • Drive Integrated Forecasting: Lead comprehensive forecasts and multi-year plans across key financial and operational drivers, including membership growth, product volumes, balances, revenue, expenses, profitability, capacity, and other critical business measures.
  • Lead and Develop Talent: Provide ongoing coaching, performance feedback, mentoring, and development opportunities that empower team members to grow, succeed, and achieve their full potential.
  • Establish Forecast Assumptions: Define, document, validate, and align assumptions, business drivers, performance targets, and planning scenarios to ensure consistency and accuracy across forecasts.
  • Build Strategic Models: Create driver-based forecasting models and scenario analyses that evaluate the impact of market conditions, member behavior, pricing strategies, product decisions, operational changes, and strategic initiatives.
  • Deliver Executive Insights: Provide senior leaders with concise, decision-ready insights regarding forecast trends, performance variances, opportunities, risks, dependencies, and recommended actions.
  • Lead Planning Cycles: Manage recurring forecasting, annual planning, and reforecasting activities by coordinating timelines, stakeholder input, quality reviews, approvals, and deliverables across a highly matrixed organization.
  • Connect Strategy to Outcomes: Align strategic priorities, product roadmaps, marketing initiatives, workforce planning, capacity planning, and investment decisions with expected financial and member outcomes.
  • Create Performance Visibility: Establish and maintain performance measurement frameworks, executive dashboards, scorecards, and reporting tools that provide meaningful visibility into organizational performance and future outlooks.
  • Partner Across the Enterprise: Collaborate closely with Finance and other business partners to support budgeting, financial projections, business cases, initiative valuation, expense management, leadership reporting, and enterprise forecast alignment.
  • Advance Analytics Capabilities: Partner with Data and Business Intelligence teams to enhance data quality, reporting automation, self-service analytics, forecasting models, and planning effectiveness.
  • Facilitate Business Alignment: Lead cross-functional planning discussions and decision-making forums that surface tradeoffs, encourage healthy debate, and drive alignment around priorities, resources, assumptions, and actions.
  • Continuously Improve Processes: Strengthen forecasting methods, planning tools, governance controls, and business processes through automation, standardization, variance analysis, back-testing, and continuous improvement efforts.
  • Strengthen Risk Awareness: Ensure forecasting and planning activities appropriately identify, monitor, assess, and communicate business, financial, operational, compliance, and execution risks in accordance with established policies and procedures.
  • Influence at the Executive Level: Develop executive and Board-ready presentations that transform complex information into compelling narratives, strategic implications, options, and recommendations.
  • Support Organizational Success: Perform additional responsibilities as assigned while contributing to enterprise-wide goals and initiatives.

This isn’t just about ticking off tasks on a list. It's about making a significant, positive change in BECU’s journey, where your contributions are valued, and your growth is continually fostered.

WHAT YOU’LL GAIN:

  • Executive Visibility: Partner directly with senior leaders and executives while influencing decisions that shape BECU's future.
  • Strategic Influence: Drive forecasting, planning, and performance management practices that impact enterprise priorities and outcomes.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with leaders across Finance, Product, Marketing, Operations, Technology, Treasury, Risk, and Enterprise Strategy.
  • Meaningful Impact: Connect business strategy, financial performance, and member outcomes in ways that directly contribute to organizational success.
  • Mission-Driven Work: Help strengthen the financial well-being of BECU members through thoughtful planning and strategic decision support.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business administration, economics, statistics, analytics, or related discipline, or equivalent work or educational experience.
  • 8 years of relevant experience in financial planning and analysis, business forecasting, strategic planning, analytics, portfolio management, or related disciplines.
  • 5 years of people leader experience.
  • Experience forecasting, planning, or analyzing consumer lending portfolios within the financial services industry.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree.
  • Knowledge of financial institution economics, products, regulatory expectations, and risk management practices.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional forecasting, annual planning, and performance management processes.
  • Advanced knowledge of driver-based forecasting, financial modeling, scenario planning, variance analysis, business cases, and performance measurement.
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize financial, product, operational, member, market, and competitive data into meaningful insights and recommendations.
  • Experience partnering with senior executives and presenting complex concepts, tradeoffs, and recommendations in concise, decision-ready form.
  • Ability to influence and gain alignment across technical, financial, product, operational, and highly matrixed teams.
  • Experience developing dashboards and management reporting; proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with enterprise planning, business intelligence, and visualization platforms.
  • Excellent leadership, facilitation, communication, writing, organization, and change management skills.

JOIN THE JOURNEY:

Ready to make a significant impact? Eager to be a part of a collaborative and innovative team where your ideas and contributions don’t just fill a role, but fuel the growth and success of BECU? This is more than a job – it’s a chance to elevate your career, skills, and future, all while contributing to the robust organizational landscape of BECU.

Embrace the opportunity to grow with us. Apply now, bring your expertise to the table, and let’s achieve excellence together at BECU. Your journey of influence, innovation, and impactful contribution starts now. #BECU #YourGrowth #BECUJourney

jobs.description:
Say hello to Hagerty

Hagerty is a company built by drivers for drivers. We put our members at the center of everything we do, and are dedicated to making it easier and more enjoyable for enthusiasts to drive and celebrate the machines they love. We’re proud to be the world’s largest insurer of collectible and enthusiast vehicles and are home to the Hagerty Drivers Club, the world’s largest car club. Our Marketplace business presents live and digital sales across the U.S. and Europe, we host a number of driving events and concours, and our award-winning automotive journalists produce the most popular car magazine globally, alongside internationally awarded videos. We’re committed to Never Stop Driving. Ready to get in the driver’s seat? Join us!

Hagerty Private Client is our dedicated division serving collectors with the most significant and irreplaceable collections — providing not just insurance, but a curated experience worthy of their passion. Private Client members interact with Hagerty across insurance, claims, membership, events, auctions, and marketing. Today, the quality and consistency of those interactions vary by team and by individual. As the Director, Private Client Experience & Standards, you will unify and define what Private Client service means, setting the standard for every function that delivers it and building a curriculum that makes that standard durable.

What you’ll do

Experience Standards & Enforcement

· Define, document, and enforce a unified Private Client experience standard covering written communications, verbal tone, response times, event protocols, and service delivery, applicable across all member-facing functions

· Partner with Private Client leadership and functional managers to develop and deliver ongoing training programs that instill service standards, brand voice, and HNW client etiquette across all teams in scope

· Establish SLAs for member-facing turnaround times across quotes, service requests, endorsements, claims communications, and a reporting cadence that makes adherence visible to leadership

· Build and maintain the Private Client Communication Playbook and Escalation Protocols, embedded in onboarding and ongoing training for every function in scope

· Partner with team leads and functional managers across claims, sales/service center, events, underwriting, and marketing to align their teams to the standard, influencing without direct authority

· Define and enforce experience standards that apply equally to the broker channel, trusted advisors (family offices, business managers, collection managers), and direct member interactions — ensuring seamless, consistent quality at every touchpoint, not just the final mile

· Establish broker-specific SLAs and communication protocols that reflect the speed, professionalism, and accuracy required when brokers are quoting, binding, or servicing high-TIV accounts on behalf of Private Client members

· Build and maintain a Broker Experience Playbook covering tone, turnaround expectations, escalation pathways, and engagement standards for all broker-mediated interactions — embedded in onboarding and ongoing training alongside the member-facing Communication Playbook


Private Client Standards Program & Cross-Team Curriculum

Architecting and leading a standards program that reaches every Hagerty team with Private Client touchpoints.

Scope of the curriculum includes:

· Private Client team members and MSC associates transitioning into the channel

· Claim adjusters handling Private Client losses

· Underwriting and endorsement teams processing high-TIV accounts

· Events and experiences staff engaged in member-facing programming

· Broad Arrow and Marketplace teams interacting with collector-sellers and buyers who are also Private Client members

· Marketing and communications teams that produce member-facing content

· Brokers and broker-support staff who are the primary point of entry for the majority of Private Client members — including training on Hagerty’s Private Client value proposition, how to position the product to HNW clients, and the service standards they can expect from Hagerty at every step

· Trusted advisors to the member (family offices, business managers, collection managers) who interact with Hagerty on behalf of the member and must receive the same quality of experience as the member themselves


Member Journey & Roadmap Development

· Map the end-to-end Private Client experience across all channels — from first broker contact through policy binding, direct member onboarding, and long-term collector engagement — identifying friction points, handoff gaps, and opportunities to exceed expectations at every stage, including interactions managed through trusted advisors

· Develop and maintain a multi-year experience roadmap aligned to business goals, member feedback, and competitive benchmarks in the HNW insurance and lifestyle services space

· Translate member and broker feedback into structured improvement programs with measurable outcomes


Segmentation & Differentiated Experience Design

· Design and implement a tiered experience model that meaningfully differentiates service delivery across Private Client's three member segments

· Develop segmentation criteria creating clear protocols and benefits that are defensible, scalable, and member-facing

· Define segment-specific proactive outreach cadences, concierge touchpoints, event invitations, and access to exclusive Hagerty services

· Ensure broker-facing communications and toolkits reflect segment distinctions so brokers can effectively position Private Client to their HNW clients


Hagerty Ecosystem Integration

A key differentiator for Hagerty Private Client is access to the broader Hagerty ecosystem. This role is responsible for weaving these assets into the member experience and training curriculum in a cohesive, high-value way:

· Broad Arrow: Auctions, Private Sales & Finance, weave auction access, private sale capabilities, and financing options into the concierge model

· Hagerty Marketplace: Integrate Marketplace access as a member benefit and collector resource, particularly for mid-tier segment members

· Events: Coordinate with the events team to create segment-appropriate invitations to owned and sponsored events (Amelia Island, Pebble Beach, private track days), ensuring elite members feel genuinely included in the Hagerty community

· Hagerty Drivers Foundation: Incorporate Hagerty's charitable mission into member touchpoints where appropriate, offering engagement opportunities aligned with collector values and legacy

· Partner with product, marketing, and partnership teams to align Private Client communications with broader Hagerty initiatives, without diluting the exclusivity of the Private Client experience

This might describe you

· Extremely experienced in High-Net-Worth client services, luxury brand management, private banking, family office advisory, or a comparable premium service environment

· Demonstrated success building and implementing client experience programs, service standards, and operational frameworks from the ground up

· Proven experience designing and personally delivering training programs, including onboarding curricula, service standards training, and cross-functional coaching

· Strong project management capability, able to independently define scope, manage cross-functional stakeholders, and deliver structured programs on time

· Deep understanding of HNW individual psychology, collector behavior, and how affluent clients prioritize relationships, trust, and exclusivity

· Genuine familiarity with collector car culture, including the motivations, community, and lifestyle that define serious automotive enthusiasts

· Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to set a high standard and coach others to it

· Experience with communication audits, quality assurance frameworks, or service excellence programs

· Comfortable operating independently in a matrixed organization with the executive presence to influence without direct authority

Over and above

· Background in specialty insurance, luxury automotive, fine art, estate management, or another asset-intensive HNW sector

· Experience designing tiered membership or loyalty programs with clear benefit differentiation by segment

· Familiarity with the auction and private sales marketplace for collector vehicles

· Prior experience working alongside philanthropy and charitable giving programs as part of a client engagement model

· Formal training in adult learning, executive coaching, or service excellence methodologies

Other things to note

  • This position is open to U.S. remote work. However, team members who reside within 20 miles of the Traverse City headquarters will follow a hybrid schedule, working from the office three days per week.
  • Familiarity with public company requirements, including Sarbanes Oxley and key regulations, if applicable. For SOX compliant roles, responsible for designing, executing, and documenting internal controls where they have been identified as owners to prevent errors in financial reporting, processes, and business operations. Including attestation to the completeness, accuracy, and compliance of all financial reporting data, where applicable.

If you reside in the following jurisdictions: Illinois, Colorado, California, District of Columbia, Hawaii, Maryland, Minnesota, Nevada, New York, or Jersey City, New Jersey, Cincinnati or Toledo, Ohio, Rhode Island, Washington, British Columbia, Canada please email for compensation, comprehensive benefits and the perks that set us apart.

At Hagerty, we share the road. We are an inclusive automotive community where all are welcomed, valued and belong regardless of race, gender, age, or car preference. We are united by our shared passion for driving, our commitment to preserve car culture for future generations and our desire to make a positive impact in the world.

Requirements

    Educational Background:

    University degree in Translation/Applied Languages/Linguistic Studies or Degree in Medicine, Biology, Biochemistry, Clinical Research, or a related life sciences field, or equivalent combination of education and experience (University degree in other fields plus 2 years of full time experience in translation; OR 5 years of full time professional experience in translating

    Industry Experience:

    Experience working at a local and/or global pharmaceutical company or Contract Research Organization (CRO — a company hired by pharma/biotech firms to conduct clinical trials and research on their behalf). This experience can come from a variety of roles, such as:

    • Pharmacovigilance specialist (monitoring and reporting drug safety and adverse events)
    • Regulatory affairs expert (managing submissions to health authorities like the FDA or EMA)

The Engineering Manager is a squad leader, people leader, and engineering steward responsible for managing delivery squads —with a shared roadmap, vision, and cross-team dependencies. In this role, you will own the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), build high-performing teams through active coaching and mentorship, and partner closely with Product, Design, and Technical Leads to deliver high-quality software that drives value for LawVu customers globally.

You lead results-driven delivery squads that operate with clear goals and ownership, fostering a high-trust environment where "blameless" problem-solving is the norm.

What you will be doing:

This is a leadership position, and the skills you bring cross a variety of different disciplines, and you will need to switch and juggle between them all.

Team Leadership

  • Build and grow the squads: hire, onboard, and develop strong engineering and QA talent, with clear performance goals, regular 1:1s, and real-time coaching that translates into visible career growth.

  • Handle HR matters and support resource/staffing planning across the squads and functions.
  • Develop communication skills across the team.

Software Development & Delivery Execution

  • Delivery is constant: uphold the SDLC, architectural best practices, and the Definition of Done, partnering with Product, Design, and Technical Leads so every sprint ships high-quality, well-tested work.
  • Keep the squad unblocked: remove technical and non-technical impediments, and own change management and stakeholder communication during incidents, supporting the Tech Lead, who leads the technical response.
  • Hit the bar: deliver against clear success criteria, quality, release frequency, security compliance, and defect rates.
  • Support the Technical Lead with guidance on architecture and solution designs aligned to the target architecture.
  • There’s no expectation for hands on coding, can pitch in, when possible, especially with the advancements with AI.

Operational Excellence

  • Keep leadership informed: flag material estimates or scope changes early, and maintain accurate, visible work status across project tools.
  • Manage stakeholders with confidence: build trusted relationships across Product, Design, and cross-functional partners, communicating progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly so stakeholders stay aligned and confident in the squad's delivery.
  • Strengthen how the team operates: surface risks, dependencies, and process gaps, and embed solid operational standards, runbooks, deployment checklists, incident management, and out-of-office coverage.

Roadmap & Strategic Planning

  • Shape technical direction: partner with Technical Leads, Architecture, and fellow Engineering Managers to prioritise technical investment and keep delivery efficient across squads.

Agile Leadership

  • Run a well-oiled squad: This means effective estimation, predictable forecasting, and delivery dates with confidence. Programmatic continual improvement with a reduced time to value.
  • Balance capacity: keep work-type allocation (features, support, tech debt) tracked and balanced, coaching the team toward continuous improvement.

Tech Debt & Quality

  • Resolve what matters most: prioritise and drive down tech debt, starting with Sev1 root causes, critical/high security issues, and high-volume support pain points, while growing automated QA coverage as a core team metric.

AI & Continuous Learning

  • Champion AI adoption & impact: embed AI-native tools like GitHub Copilot into daily workflows, track adoption as a team metric, and ensure the team invests regular time in training across AI, security, Agile, and testing.

What we need from you:

  • 8+ years of experience designing, building and shipping full stack applications; comfortable engaging across the UI, API and data layers including cloud infrastructure, CI/CD Pipelines, Object Oriented design, automated testing.
  • B.S. or equivalent in Computer Science or equivalent skills and knowledge.
  • Hands-on experience writing, reviewing, and debugging production code, with the technical credibility to guide engineering decisions.
  • Experience leading teams in the adoption of AI-native engineering workflows to improve developer productivity and quality.
  • Extensive professional software engineering experience, with a proven track record of technical maturity and delivering complex systems.
  • Working knowledge of Agile practices: user story decomposition, estimation, sprint planning, Kanban.
  • Employee management skills: coaching, performance assessment, delegation and communication.
  • Strong experience leading, coaching, and performance-managing engineers, including building and improving team capability over time.
  • Ability to make mature, objective technical decisions grounded in principles and data.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate across technical and business audiences.
  • Proven stakeholder management skills, building trust with Product, Design, and business stakeholders, and navigating competing priorities with confidence.

What sets us apart:

Why LawVu?
